wide_decoder_validation.interpretation: Every decoder output must have reached its one-hot rail before WL_EN, with the 1.5 rule. A four-stage early-PRE pass is conservative for actual16/44-stage column guards; an early-PRE failure requires the actual frozen column guard to pass. Four peripheral columns omit the slower wide PRE bar, so these are setup load coupons, not access-time or post-layout evidence.

profile: compact_control=True; w_rc=False; illustrative distributed wiring scaled from unchanged full kit xRC

dimension_floor.basis: Dimensions below 32 conservatively retain the 32x32 calibrated floor; no smaller-size timing gain is inferred

method: Reuse g15 SS physical PRE, ISO, wordline, replica, output and recovery segments; separate the observed column-control costs from row-dependent replica discharge.
Use the actual full decoder/setup coupon at each frozen row class, scaled by the largest measured same-driver historical xRC/schematic access or recovery ratio.
Resolve PRE admission and decoder setup in parallel. Read sensing uses ISO-ready; retained guards remain. No unmeasured K2 replica speed credit is taken.

Read/write completion charges twelve guard/timer stages and the larger measured preliminary C1 completion tail. Recovery covers legacy physical tails, current C1 latent timers, and the entire long decoder-setup chain reset.

At 256 columns add the recorded extracted-metal coupon PRE/WEN/ISO tail growth and the exact frozen 44-stage guard cost. Beyond 128 rows retain the largest measured positive per-row replica/restore slope.

Optional final 32x32 nominal post-layout completion records calibrate that anchor exactly. Upward error scales larger models. Downward transfer to any unmeasured shape is blocked: K2 effects do not transfer to K1, and a read-limited correction does not transfer to a write-limited width. Same-size schematic nominal/MC ratios replace preliminary sample ratios when supplied.

access_ps/cycle_ps include a separately stated assumed mismatch reserve, rounded up to integer picoseconds. The D 10% margin and 50ps rounding are each applied once in the reported period/deadline. Engineering uncertainty is separate and is not a statistical confidence interval.
limitations: No new-controller full-array timing or waveform pass is claimed at 64/128/256/512 or the joint shapes. Historical g15 data belongs to the V2.2.8 controller; 64/128 physical runs freeze unprobed cells as recorded in that baseline.
Before final 32x32 calibration the absolute values are planning estimates; they must not silently lower a production default clock.

The 20 preliminary 8x8 mismatch cases used an old unused gated-clock name collision; they are numeric calibration evidence only, not final frozen-driver qualification. Three samples per corner cannot bound a yield tail.

The 25 actual full-decoder coupons establish nominal one-hot setup closure at five corners using estimated four-column WL gate loads; they do not establish full-array access, write-completion 1.5 margins, retention, sense margin or recovery at larger sizes.
The 25%/40% bands and at least 10% mismatch reserve are explicit engineering assumptions, not measured error bars or probability guarantees.

The normal sizing profile and w_rc=True require their own calibration and are NOT covered by this compact-profile estimate. The historical ratio is a measured V2.2.8 SS comparison, not proven transferable to C1 or every corner.
Electrical behavior at corners other than SS is not simulated by this model; the measured 8x8 worst-corner ratios and wide uncertainty do not replace worst-PVT qualification.
The joint rule comparison is an event-model consistency check, not measured shape validation. Any negative slack requires a larger joint allowance before table use.
A reduced estimated period relative to an unqualified old design-table period is not a measured speedup. Unchanged/increased estimates are retained; no universal speedup is claimed.

grid_policy: Round dimensions up to the next row/column anchor, then use that explicit grid cell. Grid budgets are the monotone envelope of all20 conservative shape budgets, before the single10% policy margin and50ps rounding. The separable ladder is retained as a comparison, not used to double-count shared parallel controller paths.
report_scope: Compact-control 6T, standard2:1mux, frozenW/L; final32SS physical anchor with single physicalMCspot, largerarrays explicitly extrapolated

completion_timer_evidence.status: fixed timer projections; not timer or array qualification

definitions.write: farRWL50 to both addressed storage nodes remaining within90/10% rails
definitions.read: farSEN50 to all sense states and selectedOUT remaining within90/10% rails
definitions.available: Fixed guard4+delay8 raw time is separate from access_done time. Neither dimension-scaled guards nor positive physical WL-fall tails are credited to fixed timer stages.

limitations: A longer period cannot fix a fixed completion timer firing too early.

Larger physical timer delays use same-primitive historical32 ISO-guard ratios as an engineering assumption; these are not a proved physical lower bound. The unscaled schematic diagnostic makes this dependency visible.
Preliminary8x8 timer traces contain the old unused gated-clock name collision. Active fixed timer topology is unchanged, but this is not final frozen-driver qualification.

Write extrapolation normalizes measured low-bitline discharge by actual frozen write-driver width, then uses estimated new WEN-to-WL predrive lead. Long decoder setup may improve that lead, but a generous period itself does not.

When supplied, the nominal frozen6T cell coupon directly solves regeneration under that BL decay and WL slew, adding the nonnegative difference against measured128x128 cell90. This avoids double-counting remainingBL10 time plus a full intrinsic cell delay. Ideal coupon rails and lack of cellxRC remain engineering uncertainty.

The sense slot is extracted and has1000 mismatch samples per corner, but its output latch is schematic and rails ideal. Array differential must actually reach1.5Vbar at every sampled/mismatched sense slot; that requirement is unqualified for larger arrays.
25%/40% timing bands are engineering assumptions, not statistical bounds. Supply bounce, large-array wire skew, array mismatch and transfer between controller layouts remain unqualified.

Negative conditional margins or a failed differential requirement make a cycle budget unusable until the timer/replica policy or controller is corrected and checked. Clock enlargement is insufficient.

Slew advance uses measured90/270nm observer DC trip points with an explicit0.10VDD lower-trip reserve. This is an engineering assumption, not a measured mismatch bound. A slower rising edge cannot advance a nominal observer whose trip exceeds50%.
Predrive lead is scaled for each corner by the smaller measured legacy lead ratio and measured UnitDelayChain increment ratio toSS; the generous SS lead is not granted unchanged to fast corners.

Per-row stage suggestions use the worst corner/column deficit at a further20% shorter transferred completion delay, divided by measured minimum steady UnitDelayChain stage delay with the same20% reserve. Stage counts are timing-reference estimates, not measured corrected-array results.
